paragraphs:
Rabbi Yaakov bar Peluti.
(Or Yefliti, according to Seder HaDorot.)
In Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 2:5, Rabbi Mana (entry B in Hyman) was Rabbi Yaakov’s shoshvin (groomsman) on Sukkot.

notes.text: The printed marker ב) is retained; its note is not supplied. The natural syntax makes Rabbi Mana the shoshvin of Rabbi Yaakov.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Sukkah2:5 paragraph explicitly makes Rabbi Mana the shoshvin of Rabbi Yaakov bar Yefliti, with both titles full. This supports the reporting direction and the variant Hyman attributes to Seder HaDorot, not independent inspection of that book. The supplied ב) may letter a same-name entry or mark a note; the earlier categorical missing-footnote claim is qualified here. Its content or ordinal is not invented, and Peluti/Yefliti remain reported variants.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud and Seder HaDorot both call him Yaakov bar Yefliti and describe Rabbi Mana as his shoshvin. Hyman prints Peluti in the heading and cites the Yefliti variant. The ב) after Mana refers to Hyman’s lettered Mana entry (vol. III, pp. 885–886). That entry describes Yaakov as Mana’s shoshvin, reversing the roles given here and in the consulted Jerusalem Talmud.
